migration.notes: 51 of 51 coverage entries replayed clean (references, labels, move-result, branch offsets, register moves, register flow, return types); the battery toggle row is withheld, see migration/coverage-exclusions.json. The custom hunks are gated by migration/hunk-contracts.json plus scripts/verify_214_custom_hunks.py, which re-derives every entry from the 194 delta (instruction shape and frame growth, payload literals, the reviewed splice recomputed from the 214 upstream, the register/encoding law, the contracts, the custom-only surfaces, and the type each register provably holds where a hunk reads it) and is enforced by scripts/migrate_214.py; scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py corrupts one reviewed property at a time to prove the gate goes red. The type walk is also run over the pristine 214 tree (--type-flow-control), which reports nothing; it is what the first 214 build failed on (VerifyError in hi1.d), and scripts/port_214_candidate.py now mirrors a customization's register rename onto the line the port keeps, recorded per line in migration/port-report.json. A second device crash came from the other direction: a `replace` hunk carried the register numbering of the frame it was written in (`Ljk5;->c` handed the `Ljava/lang/String;` slot v14 to `Lcom/box/app/vpn/VpnBridge;->key(Lbr5;)I` because 194 kept that enum in v14 and 214 moved it to v15), so scripts/port_214_candidate.py now also re-spells a replaced line's operands from the two versions of the line it replaces (1 line, recorded in migration/port-report.json under registerRealignments), and the type-flow gate was widened from "uncast Object in a narrowed slot" to any mismatch it can prove from this tree's class hierarchy - with the pristine 214 tree still reporting nothing.
